- Corn leaf (upper surface)
- Numerous very small, scattered orange/yellowish-orange dots across the leaf surface
- One larger tan/brown oval lesion lower-left
- Pustules appear small and densely scattered

Top candidates: **Common_rust** vs **Southern_rust** — the small orange dots suggest rust. Let me compare reference images.

The test image pustules are small, light orange/yellow-orange, scattered on the upper surface. Southern rust reference matches better (small, densely packed, orange, upper surface). Let me check a couple more candidates.
Physoderma has banding + dark midrib spots (not matching). Eyespot has halos with tan centers (not matching). Let me view two more to confirm.

Tar spot has raised black spots (very different). Holcus spot has large discrete white/tan round spots (not matching).

**Summary of evidence:**

- Test image: Very small, scattered orange/yellow-orange pustules on the **upper leaf surface** of a corn leaf, with one larger oval tan lesion
- **Southern rust** matches: small, circular-oval, light orange, primarily upper surface, densely scattered
- **Common rust** doesn't match: larger, more brick-red, oval ~1/8" pustules on *both* surfaces
- Physoderma, Eyespot, Tar spot, Holcus all ruled out by morphology
